tag: Episode 32 · The Owner of the Black Feather
title: The Owner of the Black Feather

beats.t: The iron-walled room fell silent. Only the black threads binding Wu Qu stirred, pulsing like a heartbeat.
I know no one named Museong. I am the keeper of the Career gate.
Liar. You scrape the floor with your right big toe before you answer. You did it every time you went onstage.
The crow's claw stopped dead against the floor. It had been just about to scrape the iron.
(It really was about to. Moka remembered even that.)
The otter's memories are subject to confiscation. The crime of laughter, the crime of rhythm, and the crime of remembering.
Then take them all. But take off your mask first.
The black feather in the crow's chest gave a violent throb. The crow clutched its chest. Its wingtips shivered.
The feather is resisting. Hearing his name seems to shake its roots.
Keep calling his name, Mr. Otter. Not loudly. Just clearly.
Museong.
A hairline crack crossed the mask, running from forehead to chin.
Museong. The day after the sunrise concert, I went to your house. I couldn't knock.
The mask split and fell. It struck the iron floor in two pieces. The cloak's collar slid down.
Underneath was a boy's face. About Yeoni's age, perhaps a little younger. Dark hollows lay beneath his eyes. He looked as though he hadn't slept in a long time.
...I know you didn't knock. I saw you through the window. You stood there for ages, then left.
You should have come out.
I thought you might laugh again if I did.
Moka's tail slumped to the floor. The tail that always kept time made no sound.
Years earlier, on the Island of Expression. The dawn stage at the Sunrise Festival. Before the sun had stopped at noon, when the far edge of the sea was just turning red.
A boy stood onstage with his eyes closed. The audience was packed. He always sang with his eyes closed because looking at the crowd made him nervous.
Rise, sun. Today's first song is for you.
The drum sounded. The boy took a deep breath. And on the very first line, his voice cracked. Like a rooster crowing. Loud enough to carry to the farthest edge of the dawn sea.
Laughter burst from the front row. One person laughed, then the next. It spread backward like a wave.
A small otter sat in the middle of the front row, holding a skewer among his friends. He was laughing too.
The boy opened his eyes. For the first time since stepping onto the stage, he looked at the audience. Laughing faces. And among them, a familiar otter's face.
The boy sang to the final line, his voice still cracked. Then he never went onstage again.
...I laughed too. Right in the front.
Moka.
All my friends were laughing. Wouldn't it have been weird if I didn't? So I laughed. One second. No, maybe two.
Three seconds.
Right. Three. You counted.
Moka set down his skewer. The metal skewer he never let out of his hand. Then he looked straight at the boy.
I'm sorry. For those three seconds. I've wanted to make up for them ever since. I didn't know how, so all I did was grill skewers.
(The tune Moka always hummed over the coals. It was this boy's song.)
Museong's lips trembled. He tried to say something. But the feather in his chest moved first. The black threads jerked tight.
Ghh...!
A low, cold voice seeped from the feather. It wasn't the boy's voice.
An apology for three seconds, to repay years of silence? Otter, your price is wrong.
Black Moon!
Ask the boy what I promised when I gave him the feather.
The night of the sunrise concert. A seaside hill at the edge of the island. The boy sat alone, his throat hoarse.
I wish I'd never sung at all.
Something settled through the sound of the waves. A single black feather. Though there was no wind, it landed precisely on the boy's knees.
I will make sure your voice never cracks again.
...Really?
Simply remove every voice that could crack. Yours, and everyone else's. If no one sings, no one can mock you.
The boy pushed the feather into his chest. Warmth spread instead of pain. He felt as though no one would recognize him anymore. His hunched shoulders relaxed.
That night, the boy's voice entered the feather. From the following day, the island's songs began disappearing one by one.
First, a market seller's bargaining song. Then a hum at the washing place. Then the children's skipping songs. Every vanished song went to the same place: the black feather in the boy's chest.
The more songs the feather ate, the larger it grew. Black feathers sprouted on the boy's arms. Wings emerged from his back. One morning, a crow stood in his mirror.
Well done. Now there is no one left to mock you. No one sings anymore.
...Then why is it so quiet? So quiet it hurts my ears?
That is peace.
Museong stopped there and lowered his head. No one spoke. Only the sound of rust falling from the iron walls remained.
That's why you banned singing on the Island of Expression. The feather wanted it, not you.
No. I wanted it too. At first, I really liked it. An island where nobody laughed. I made that.
But laughter wasn't the only thing that disappeared. The applause went too. Because no one sang.
The hands of the people who laughed probably clapped too. Can you cut out only the memories that hurt?
(His own arm is like that, and he's still worrying about the boy first.)
The cat mister is right. By the time I realized it, the feather had already put down roots in my throat.
He called you mister.
...This is not the moment.
Museong sank to his knees. Threads from the feather coiled around his neck. Every breath made a metallic sound.
I understand now. That feather is his throat. His breath, his voice—everything is inside it.
Then if we pull it out...
His breath comes out with it. He dies. Drawing it into my Void would have the same result.
But if we leave it, Wu Qu will be erased. At noon in three days.
That means you'll be erased too!
Neo didn't answer. The gray spreading to his neck rippled with each breath. A metallic rasp mingled with the end of every inhalation.
Pull it out.
What?
Pull it out. Your cat will live. Wu Qu will too. All the confiscated light will return.
I ended on that hill years ago anyway. The feather is only breathing for me now.
Don't talk nonsense!
Otter. You just apologized. That's enough. It really is.
Yeoni looked at Neo, then Museong. Their breathing made the same sound. Metal. The sound of something strangling them.
(Throw one away to save the other. Black Moon's favorite arithmetic.)
Yeoni. Don't worry about me. You make the decision.
(A decision. Lian Zhen said fire rots if you only cage it. That my silence can hurt people.)
Yeoni had been holding their fire back all this time. Shouting hurt Neo. But while they held it in, everyone was lining up to pay the price alone.
I'm not pulling it out.
Then the cat will...
The cat won't be erased. Neither will Wu Qu. And you won't die. All three.
Such greed, vessel. The scales do not tip that way.
Fire rose in Yeoni's chest. This time it didn't explode. It was small and steady, no larger than a lantern flame.
Then I won't use your scales. They always tip toward you.
Yeoni looked at Neo. He hadn't flinched. The gray hadn't spread any farther either. Their eyes met for a moment. There might be another way.
...It doesn't hurt.
(Because I spoke instead of shouting? Because I lit it instead of making it explode?)
We neither pull it out nor erase anything. That leaves one option.
We change it. The Obstruction.
Obstruction Transformation into Prosperity Transformation. Turn a blocked place into one that flows. It works in theory. Though no one has tried it.
'In theory' is the scariest phrase there is.
True. Every compatibility reading works in theory too.
(They said Obstruction was like a debt. A place that stagnates because it never received what it was owed.)
What Museong never received. I think I know what it is.
Everyone looked at Yeoni, even Museong. Yeoni gently nudged Moka's back.
Applause. What he didn't get onstage that day.
...I don't need applause. That couldn't possibly remove the feather.
No, it makes sense. If Obstruction marks something unreceived, receiving it could release the blockage. But it has to be real. Pity applause doesn't enter the ledger.
Real applause. How do we do that?
You always hummed over the coals. I'm the only one who's heard that song all the way through. It was pretty good.
You heard it? Since when?
The first day. Your rapping was awful, but that song was good.
Moka looked at Museong for a long time. Then he tapped the floor once with his tail. Tap.
At that moment, the entire room shook. Rust rained from the iron walls. A bell rang beyond the ceiling. Once. Twice.
Three days is too long. Noon is now.
He's moved the time forward! Wu Qu is starting to be erased!
Lines of light went out one by one in the bound star. Neo fell to his knees. The bell rang a third time. When the twelfth bell rang, it would be noon.
